Recycle Hack - Well, anyone who owns a Samsung French Door Refrig with a POS Ice Room Ice Maker knows that even after applying all the fixes, they'll still be hair-dryer defrosting it, every ~3 months; I've got it down to ~15 minutes now. So instead of buying a new refrigerator-with-ice-maker-in-the-freezer-drawer (at C0stc0), I decided to limp it along another year and buy another filter. There's just the two of us in the household and I've calculated we dispense <300gal through the filter annually PLUS we have a clean water supply, so I ignore the 6 month reminder and replace it every December.
The filter is a simple plastic 1/4" thick, two piece plastic cartridge with 3 rubber o-rings, housing the carbon-filter insert. It's not difficult to disassemble the filter for recycling/disposal:
1) remove the o-rings with an awl or precision mini bladed screwdriver. shake out the water.
2) clamp the filter in a vise or brace appropriately
3) (hack)saw 1/4" deep around the diameter at the cartridge seam, about 1/3 up from the bottom.
4) discard the carbon-filter insert and recycle the two plastic cartridge pieces.
Maybe call your recycler and confirm they recycle Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) (7).
Remember to run 3 gallons of water through your new filter. Maybe water the plants, fill a toilet tank, or clean the sinks and use it for rinse water.

Time For A Change....Only Not. - I have had this dish rack for the last 8 years and it has endured the trials of drying LOTS of dishes for my family of 11. Gradually, some of the kids have grown up and moved out, but this dish rack continues to do the job for the 2 that are still home, my husband, and myself. One piece of plastic that divides the dishes is now broken and the most vigorous scrubbing no longer gets it clean, so I was more than a little excited when my husband suggested that we finally retire the old one. Surely there must be some major advances in dish rack technology over the last decade, I thought. But no. After spending way too much time researching what is on the market, it appears that this model remains the best choice for people who need large dish racks with lots of flexibility in how it can be loaded. Ratings for other brands were significantly lower even for models five times the price and from well known kitchen product manufacturers. So, I will be sticking with the tried and true, although this decade I will going with the red to match my cherry Le Creuset pans and KitchenAid small appliances. Maybe I will have to consider designing a functional large dish rack myself because there is clearly a market.

I ended up Liking this Machine, it works well - How to Wash Clothing with this Machine (Short)

I filled it up with a bucket. When you add your clothes make sure there is enough water so they float around when moved by your hand.

Filling : the water supply must be higher than the inlet, or use a bucket. Easy on the soap... you will need to rinse the soap out of the clothes. Mine was about half full. Wash at setting 15

Drain the wash cycle when done and filled again with water for rinse using half the time as wash. Wring a bit of water out of each clothing as you add clothes to the spin section. Set Spin to 5

The spin cycle is quiet and doesn't shake the machine and gets the clothes a bit damp. Keep spinning until very little water comes out of drain. Clothing should be slightly damp.

Better than washing clothes in a laundry room. No more unwashed laundry!

Actionable bundle of technology - The primary purpose of this AcuRite Indoor Air Quality Monitor is an alert to turn on the humidifier for sensitive family members. It's dimmable and legible. The sampling rate and screen update are appropriate.

Depending on your use, this monitor measures @PM2.5. It's an appropriate indoor green/yellow/red light monitor. @PM2.5 ≤ 12µ = green light. Yellow light between 13-35. >35? Deepening shades of red ... until you can't see color, then like-2000 years in the future, some kid will be digging a hole and strike a void, someone will pour plaster of Paris in the void and you'll live in fame, slain by flaming hot particles just like Pompeii. @PM2.5 the results are comparable to the Air Quality Index (AQI) as locally reported by NOAA.

Relative humidity (RH%) is heuristically linked to PM2.5. The higher the RH%, the lower the PM2.5. The lower the RH%, the higher the PM2.5 reading. I’ve noticed that an interior RH% ≈ 50% displays 1-5 ppm.

As a note to ‘bunny suit’ people, PM2.5 is not the metric for comparisons to ISO cleanroom levels. This monitor might suggest 1-5 ppm, but, my living room is NOT class 10 ... given rugs, etc, it can't be made to get to class 100,000.

Twenty years ago, this sensor was a high-$ industrial proposition and hardly for home use. However, Acurite has packaged a bundle of technology here to deliver excellent value for money.

Nice filter that works with almost any container, bad pitcher - We mostly buy bottled water or when available fill our water bottles at the machines in front of grocery stores. The pitcher is a serious disappointment to me. If were rating it alone, it'd get 1 star. The spout that closes for pouring has a gap in that allows water to pour out even when closed -- though it doesn't snap closed so if you bump the pitcher a little the spout flaps all around. The plastic feels cheap. It really need a different lid that doesn't pop off so easily. That's the bad.

The good is the filter itself is easy to use. It can be used in almost any pitcher or bottle you have at home. In fact If it's possible, I'd recommend buying the filter section without the pitcher. It has markings so you can see what month you starting using the filter. Although you CAN filter water fast, if you're not fond of wasting water I'd actually do it at a slower steady stream as the filter itself does not hold a lot of water so a lot of water is literally going down the drain as it pours out over the filter. At a slower pace I filled the pitched quite a bit slower but wasted a lot less.

In the end, I'd recommend the filter itself but not the pitcher.

If you are repairing your dishwasher latch and handle assembly, be sure this is the correct part. My original was white, but it's now only manufactured with a black handle. Assure that the power is cut to your dishwasher to avoid electrocution. Have your torx t20 bit in a driver or screwdriver because you need it to remove the 11 screws holding the interior door to the exterior door. The two screws at the center of the upper edge hold this piece in place, so they should be the last two you remove and the first two you secure upon completion. The entire process from start to finish took about 10 minutes, including the time it took to identify the circuit to cut.
